  <section id="testcontainers-python">
<h1>
testcontainers-python
<a class="headerlink" href="#testcontainers-python" title="Link to this heading">¶</a>
</h1>
<a class="reference external image-reference" href="https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-python/actions/workflows/ci-core.yml">

<img alt="https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/testcontainers.svg" src="https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/testcontainers.svg">
</a>
<a class="reference external image-reference" href="http://testcontainers-python.readthedocs.io/en/latest/?badge=latest">

</a>
<p>testcontainers-python facilitates the use of Docker containers for functional and integration testing. The collection of packages currently supports the following features.</p>
<div class="toctree-wrapper compound">

<section id="getting-started">
<h2>
Getting Started
<a class="headerlink" href="#getting-started" title="Link to this heading">¶</a>
</h2>
<div class="highlight-pycon notranslate">
<div class="highlight">
<pre><span></span>
<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">testcontainers.postgres</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">PostgresContainer</span>
<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">sqlalchemy</span>

<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">PostgresContainer</span>
<span class="p">(</span>
<span class="s2">"postgres:16"</span>
<span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">postgres</span>
<span class="p">:</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>    <span class="n">psql_url</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">postgres</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">get_connection_url</span>
<span class="p">()</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>    <span class="n">engine</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sqlalchemy</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">create_engine</span>
<span class="p">(</span>
<span class="n">psql_url</span>
<span class="p">)</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>    <span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">engine</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">begin</span>
<span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">connection</span>
<span class="p">:</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>        <span class="n">version</span>
<span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">connection</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">execute</span>
<span class="p">(</span>
<span class="n">sqlalchemy</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">text</span>
<span class="p">(</span>
<span class="s2">"SELECT version()"</span>
<span class="p">))</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">fetchone</span>
<span class="p">()</span>
<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="n">version</span>
<span class="go">'PostgreSQL 16...'</span>
</pre>
</div>
</div>
<p>
The snippet above will spin up the current latest version of a postgres database in a container. The 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">get_connection_url()</span>
</code>
 convenience method returns a 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">sqlalchemy</span>
</code>
 compatible url (using the 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">psycopg2</span>
</code>
 driver per default) to connect to the database and retrieve the database version.
</p>
<div class="highlight-pycon notranslate">
<div class="highlight">
<pre><span></span>
<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">testcontainers.postgres</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">PostgresContainer</span>
<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">psycopg</span>

<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">PostgresContainer</span>
<span class="p">(</span>
<span class="s2">"postgres:16"</span>
<span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">driver</span>
<span class="o">=</span>
<span class="kc">None</span>
<span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">postgres</span>
<span class="p">:</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>    <span class="n">psql_url</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">postgres</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">get_connection_url</span>
<span class="p">()</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>    <span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">psycopg</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">connect</span>
<span class="p">(</span>
<span class="n">psql_url</span>
<span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">connection</span>
<span class="p">:</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>        <span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">connection</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">cursor</span>
<span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">cursor</span>
<span class="p">:</span>
<span class="gp">... </span>            <span class="n">version</span>
<span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">cursor</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">execute</span>
<span class="p">(</span>
<span class="s2">"SELECT version()"</span>
<span class="p">)</span>
<span class="o">.</span>
<span class="n">fetchone</span>
<span class="p">()</span>
<span class="gp">>>> </span>
<span class="n">version</span>
<span class="go">'PostgreSQL 16...'</span>
</pre>
</div>
</div>
<p>
This snippet does the same, however using a specific version and the driver is set to None, to influence the 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">get_connection_url()</span>
</code>
 convenience method to not include a driver in the URL (e.g. for compatibility with 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">psycopg</span>
</code>
 v3).
</p>
<p>
Note, that the 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">sqlalchemy</span>
</code>
 and 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">psycopg</span>
</code>
 packages are no longer a dependency of 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">testcontainers[postgres]</span>
</code>
 and not needed to launch the Postgres container. Your project therefore needs to declare a dependency on the used driver and db access methods you use in your code.
</p>
<p>
By default, Testcontainers will search for the container via the gateway IP. You can manually specify your own IP with the environment variable 
<cite>TESTCONTAINERS_HOST_OVERRIDE</cite>
.
</p>
</section>
<section id="installation">
<h2>
Installation
<a class="headerlink" href="#installation" title="Link to this heading">¶</a>
</h2>
<p>
The suite of testcontainers packages is available on 
<a class="reference external" href="https://pypi.org/project/testcontainers/">PyPI</a>
,
the package can be installed using 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">pip</span>
</code>
.
</p>
<p>
Version 
<cite>4.0.0</cite>
 onwards we do not support the 
<cite>testcontainers-*</cite>
 packages as it is unsustainable to maintain ownership.
</p>
<p>
Instead packages can be installed by specifying 
<a class="reference external" href="https://setuptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/setuptools.html#declaring-extras-optional-features-with-their-own-dependencies">extras</a>
, e.g., 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">pip</span> <span class="pre">install</span> <span class="pre">testcontainers[postgres]</span>
</code>
.
</p>
<p>Please note, that community modules are supported on a best-effort basis and breaking changes DO NOT create major versions in the package.
Therefore, only the package core is strictly following SemVer. If your workflow is broken by a minor update, please look at the changelogs for guidance.</p>
</section>
<section id="custom-containers">
<h2>
Custom Containers
<a class="headerlink" href="#custom-containers" title="Link to this heading">¶</a>
</h2>
<p>
Crafting containers that are based on custom images is supported by the 
<cite>core</cite>
 module. Please check the 
<a class="reference external" href="core/README.html">core documentation</a>
 for more information.
</p>
<p>This allows you to create containers from images that are not part of the modules provided by testcontainers-python.</p>
<p>
For common use cases, you can also use the generic containers provided by the 
<cite>testcontainers-generic</cite>
 module. Please check the 
<a class="reference external" href="modules/generic/README.html">generic documentation</a>
 for more information.
(example: 
<cite>ServerContainer</cite>
 for running a FastAPI server)
</p>
</section>
<section id="docker-in-docker-dind">
<h2>
Docker in Docker (DinD)
<a class="headerlink" href="#docker-in-docker-dind" title="Link to this heading">¶</a>
</h2>
<p>When trying to launch Testcontainers from within a Docker container, e.g., in continuous integration testing, two things have to be provided:</p>
<ol class="arabic simple">
<li>
<p>
The container has to provide a docker client installation. Either use an image that has docker pre-installed (e.g. the 
<a class="reference external" href="https://hub.docker.com/_/docker">official docker images</a>
) or install the client from within the 
<cite>Dockerfile</cite>
 specification.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
The container has to have access to the docker daemon which can be achieved by mounting 
<cite>/var/run/docker.sock</cite>
 or setting the 
<cite>DOCKER_HOST</cite>
 environment variable as part of your 
<cite>docker run</cite>
 command.
</p>
</li>
</ol>
</section>
<section id="private-docker-registry">
<h2>
Private Docker registry
<a class="headerlink" href="#private-docker-registry" title="Link to this heading">¶</a>
</h2>
<p>
Using a private docker registry requires the 
<cite>DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG</cite>

<a class="reference external" href="https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/login/#credential-helpers">official documentation</a>
</p>
<p>The value of this variable should be a JSON string containing the authentication information for the registry.</p>
<p>Example:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate">
<div class="highlight">
<pre><span></span>
<span class="nv">DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG</span>
<span class="o">=</span>
<span class="s1">'{"auths": {"https://myregistry.com": {"auth": "dXNlcm5hbWU6cGFzc3dvcmQ="}}}'</span>
</pre>
</div>
</div>
<p>In order to generate the JSON string, you can use the following command:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate">
<div class="highlight">
<pre><span></span>
<span class="nb">echo</span>
<span class="w"> </span>
-n
<span class="w"> </span>
<span class="s1">'{"auths": {"<url>": {"auth": "'</span>
<span class="k">$(</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span>
<span class="w"> </span>
-n
<span class="w"> </span>
<span class="s2">"<username>:<password>"</span>
<span class="w"> </span>
<span class="p">|</span>
<span class="w"> </span>
base64
<span class="w"> </span>
-w
<span class="w"> </span>
<span class="m">0</span>
<span class="k">)</span>
<span class="s1">'"}}}'</span>
</pre>
</div>
</div>

<section id="package-structure">
<h3>
Package Structure
<a class="headerlink" href="#package-structure" title="Link to this heading">¶</a>
</h3>
<p>
Testcontainers is a collection of 
<a class="reference external" href="https://peps.python.org/pep-0420/">implicit namespace packages</a>

to decouple the development of different extensions,
e.g., 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">testcontainers[mysql]</span>
</code>
 and 
<code class="code docutils literal notranslate">
<span class="pre">testcontainers[postgres]</span>
</code>
 for MySQL and PostgreSQL database containers, respectively.
</p>
<p>The folder structure is as follows:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate">
<div class="highlight">
<pre><span></span>
modules

<span class="c1"># One folder per feature.</span>
<span class="o">[</span>
feature
<span class="w"> </span>
name
<span class="o">]</span>
<span class="w">    </span>
<span class="c1"># Folder without __init__.py for implicit namespace packages.</span>
<span class="w">    </span>
testcontainers

<span class="w">        </span>
<span class="c1"># Implementation as namespace package with __init__.py.</span>
<span class="w">        </span>
<span class="o">[</span>
feature
<span class="w"> </span>
name
<span class="o">]</span>
<span class="w">            </span>
__init__.py

<span class="w">            </span>
<span class="c1"># Other files for this</span>
<span class="w">            </span>
...

<span class="w">    </span>
<span class="c1"># Tests for the feature.</span>
<span class="w">    </span>
tests

<span class="w">        </span>
test_
<span class="o">[</span>
some_aspect_for_the_feature
<span class="o">]</span>
.py

<span class="w">        </span>
...

<span class="w">    </span>
<span class="c1"># README for this feature.</span>
<span class="w">    </span>
README.rst

</pre>
</div>
</div>
</section>
